title: Lens Optics Demo with Save/Load State
prompt:
Create a single HTML file with an interactive lens optics education demo using Three.js and GLTFLoader. The scene simulates a thin converging lens on an optical bench.

## Scene Setup
- Use a perspective camera at position (0, 5, 20) looking at the origin.
- Add ambient light (intensity 0.5) and a directional light at (10, 10, 10) with intensity 0.8.
- Create a flat rectangular plane (50x0.2x2) as the optical bench along the Z-axis, colored #444444, centered at y=0.
- Draw a thin vertical plane (0.1 wide, 4 tall) at z=0 colored #88ccff with opacity 0.5 (transparent) to represent the LENS. The lens has a focal length stored in state, initially 5.0 units.
- Load the 'Avocado.glb' model using GLTFLoader. Scale it to roughly 1.5 units tall. Place it at z = -12 (object side of lens). This is the 'object' on the optical bench. It should be draggable along the Z-axis only (constrained to range z=-25 to z=-2).
- Compute and display a SCALED IMAGE of the Avocado on the image side using the thin lens equation: 1/f = 1/do + 1/di, where do = |object.z| (positive), di = image distance. The image should appear at z = +di. The magnification m = -di/do determines the image scale (negative means inverted). Clone or mirror the Avocado model for the image, apply scaleY = m (negative flips it), scaleX = |m|, scaleZ = |m|. If di is negative (virtual image), hide the image.
- Draw ray lines (THREE.Line) from the object tip through the lens showing: (1) a ray parallel to axis bending through focal point, (2) a ray through the center of the lens going straight, (3) a ray through the near focal point bending parallel. Use yellow color for rays. Update rays in real-time as object moves.

## UI / HUD
- Add a top-left HUD panel (HTML overlay, id='hud-panel') showing:
  - Object distance (do) with id='hud-do'
  - Image distance (di) with id='hud-di'
  - Magnification (m) with id='hud-mag'
  - Focal length (f) with id='hud-focal'
  - A label showing 'Real Image' or 'Virtual Image' with id='hud-image-type'
- Add buttons:
  - 'Increase Focal Length' (id='btn-focal-up'): increases f by 1.0, max 15
  - 'Decrease Focal Length' (id='btn-focal-down'): decreases f by 1.0, min 2
  - 'Save State' (id='btn-save'): saves current state to localStorage key 'lensOpticsSave'
  - 'Load State' (id='btn-load'): loads state from localStorage and restores scene
  - 'Reset' (id='btn-reset'): resets to initial state (object at z=-12, f=5)
  - 'Toggle Rays' (id='btn-toggle-rays'): shows/hides ray lines

## Keyboard Controls
- Arrow Up/Down: move object along Z-axis by 0.5 units (clamped to -25...-2)
- 'R' key: toggle ray visibility
- 'S' key: save state
- 'L' key: load state

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with these fields, updated every frame:
- objectZ: current z position of the avocado object (negative number)
- focalLength: current focal length
- objectDistance: do = Math.abs(objectZ) (positive)
- imageDistance: di computed from thin lens equation (can be negative for virtual)
- magnification: m = -di/do
- imageVisible: boolean, true if real image (di > 0)
- imageZ: z position of image (di when real, 0 when virtual/hidden)
- raysVisible: boolean
- savedStateExists: boolean, true if localStorage has 'lensOpticsSave'
- avocadoLoaded: boolean, true once GLB model is loaded
- rayCount: number of ray lines in scene (should be 3 when visible, 0 when hidden)
- imageScaleY: the Y scale applied to the image model
- hudDoValue: parseFloat of the hud-do element text
- hudDiValue: parseFloat of the hud-di element text
- hudMagValue: parseFloat of the hud-mag element text
- stateVersion: integer incremented each time state is saved (starts at 0)

## Physics / Optics Constraints
- Thin lens equation: 1/f = 1/do + 1/di must hold at all times
- Magnification: m = -di/do
- When do < f, image is virtual (di < 0), image should be hidden
- All computed values must be finite (no NaN, no Infinity when do != f)
- When do equals f exactly, handle gracefully (hide image, set di to Infinity or very large)

## Save/Load
- Save: store {objectZ, focalLength, raysVisible, stateVersion} as JSON in localStorage
- Load: parse JSON, restore objectZ (move avocado), restore focalLength, restore raysVisible, recompute everything
- After load, stateVersion should match the saved value
physics_constraints: Thin lens equation 1/f = 1/do + 1/di must hold. Magnification m = -di/do. Real images form when do > f (di > 0). Virtual images when do < f (di < 0). All values must remain finite and NaN-free except when do = f (handle as edge case).
